title: Next bridges cover 36 of 99 backend operations and next.config.mjs declares no rewrites, so `npm run dev` serves a product where 40 client-called API routes 404
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md describes `frontend/app/api/` as '28 backend bridge routes' and Next as 'the sole production frontend'; the dynasty-data bridge's own comment says the bridges 'handle the dev flow (no nginx in front)'. The implication is that dev and production serve the same product.
observed: There are 36 bridge route.js files against 99 unique backend method+path operations (openapi.json reports 100 because /api/health also carries an auto-generated HEAD). All 36 bridges do have a backend counterpart, so no bridge is orphaned — but 63 backend operations have no bridge, and 40 of those are fetched directly by client code. next.config.mjs declares distDir, turbopack.root and exactly one redirects() entry; it declares no rewrites(). `npm run dev` is `next dev -p 3000` with nothing in front. Measured against the running stack with a valid session: /api/health, /api/leagues, /api/user/state, /api/terminal, /api/movers, /api/data/rank-history, /api/ros/player-values, /api/custom-alerts and /api/data all return 404 on :3000 while returning 200 through the edge proxy on :3001 and directly on :8000. Only the bridged alias /api/dynasty-data returns 200 on :3000. This is not hypothetical: the audit harness had to stand up a separate nginx-equivalent proxy on :3001 because the first browser capture against :3000 was full of /api/* 404s plus a 'buildRows received a payload with zero backend rank stamps' console error that production never produces.

reproduction.command: for r in /api/health /api/leagues /api/user/state /api/terminal /api/movers /api/data /api/dynasty-data; do printf '%-26s %s %s %s\n' $r $(curl -s -m 25 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H "Cookie: jason_session=$SID" http://127.0.0.1:3000$r) $(curl -s -m 60 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H "Cookie: jason_session=$SID" http://127.0.0.1:3001$r) $(curl -s -m 60 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000$r); done
reproduction.expected: Same status from :3000 (Next) and :3001 (production topology) for every route the client calls.

numericProof.formula: unbridgedButClientCalled = |{routes with a fetch() call site in frontend/ outside app/api/}| - |{routes with a matching frontend/app/api/**/route.js}|

userImpact: A developer running the documented dev command sees a materially different, broken application: no terminal, no team switcher, no user state, no ROS panel, no movers, no rank history. Bugs get chased in dev that do not exist in prod, and prod bugs cannot be reproduced in dev. It also means the resilience code in the 264-line dynasty-data bridge (disk-snapshot fallback, per-chunk idle abort) is exercised only where it does not matter.

priorFinding.note: The prior finding named three ops pages and counted 30 route.js files. At HEAD e96c06ef there are 36 bridges and the gap is 63 unbridged operations, 40 of them client-called — an order of magnitude larger than reported, and the root cause (no rewrites() in next.config.mjs) was not named.

whatWorks: Production is correct: nginx routes every /api/ to FastAPI, so the bridge gap is invisible to users. All 36 bridges do point at a real backend route — there are no orphan bridges. The e2e suite sidesteps the issue by keeping playwright baseURL on :8000.
rootCause: Bridges were added one at a time as individual pages needed them, instead of one catch-all `rewrites()` entry mapping /api/:path* to BACKEND_API_URL. There is no test that asserts dev/prod route parity.
requiredRepair: Add `async rewrites() { return [{ source: '/api/:path*', destination: `${process.env.BACKEND_API_URL || 'http://127.0.0.1:8000'}/api/:path*` }] }` to next.config.mjs (Next applies rewrites only after no route.js matches, so the 36 existing bridges keep winning), then delete the bridges that add nothing over a proxy. Pin with a test that every /api/ path referenced by frontend/ resolves under `next dev`.
dependencies: Interacts with PRIOR-A06-F10 (bridges forward cookies inconsistently) — a single rewrite removes that class of divergence too.

title: GET /api/gameplan exposes the entire src/roster_intel roster-intelligence engine and no page, component or script calls it
claimUnderTest: server.py's docstring calls /api/gameplan 'The API surface over src/roster_intel/ — analyze_roster, the per-position profiles, the five-state competitive window, both target engines, the partner model, and (on request) the Trade Package Generator's Pareto frontier.' A route described as the API surface for a subsystem implies a consumer.
observed: grep across every .js/.jsx under frontend/ (excluding node_modules and .next) returns exactly one hit for 'gameplan': a comment on line 32 of frontend/app/api/valuation/league-adjusted/route.js explaining that the overlay reuses gameplan's cached league bundle internally. There is no frontend/app/api/gameplan bridge directory. No script, workflow, systemd unit or nginx config references the path. The only callers are tests/api/test_gameplan_endpoint.py, tests/api/test_private_auth.py and tests/api/test_league_adjusted_endpoint.py. A bare authenticated GET returns 400 because `team` cannot be resolved for the e2e user, so even the smoke path is untested by any live client. The engine's code is not dead — /api/valuation/league-adjusted reaches parts of it — but the ROUTE, and the needs/window/targets/partners/Pareto-frontier outputs it alone exposes, reach no user.

reproduction.command: grep -rn 'gameplan' /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/frontend --include='*.js' --include='*.jsx' | grep -v node_modules | grep -v '\.next' ; ls /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/frontend/app/api/gameplan 2>&1 ; curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/gameplan
reproduction.expected: At least one page or component fetching /api/gameplan.
reproduction.actual: 1 hit, and it is a comment. `ls: cannot access .../frontend/app/api/gameplan: No such file or directory`. Route returns 400.

userImpact: Every answer this engine computes — positional needs, the five-state competitive window, buy/sell targets, ranked trade partners, the Pareto package frontier — is unavailable to any user. Users instead get the /phases contention label, which PRIOR-A18-F00 measured as giving the SAME team the opposite verdict, with no way to see the second opinion.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced exactly at HEAD e96c06ef: one grep hit, a comment, and no bridge directory. Adds the runtime observation that a bare authenticated GET 400s.

whatWorks: The route is registered, auth-gated, league-scoped and test-covered; src/api/gameplan.py's cached league bundle is genuinely reused by /api/valuation/league-adjusted, so the underlying package is not dead code.
rootCause: The backend engine shipped ahead of its UI and the UI was never built. Nothing fails when a route has no consumer, so nothing surfaced it.
requiredRepair: Either build the consumer (the natural home is /rosters or a per-team page — see W01-F007) or retire the route and keep the internal helpers that /api/valuation/league-adjusted uses.
dependencies: W01-F007 (no private team page) — gameplan is per-team and has nowhere to live until one exists.

title: Sixteen backend routes have no caller outside the test suite, including six /api/scaffold/* introspection routes and POST /api/test-alert which nothing references at all
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md's API table advertises /api/scaffold/status, /api/scaffold/raw and /api/scaffold/identity as first-class endpoints ('Pipeline status', 'Raw source snapshots', 'Identity mappings'), implying they are part of the working product.
observed: 16 of 99 backend operations (16.2%) have zero callers in frontend code, zero bridge consumers, zero references in .github/workflows, deploy/ or scripts/, and are referenced only by tests — or, for four of them, by nothing at all. The complete list is in the artifact. POST /api/test-alert has literally zero references anywhere in the repository including tests. GET /api/metrics is public and has no in-repo consumer (no dashboard, no workflow, no timer) — it is plausibly scraped by an external monitor, so it is classified ops rather than dead. Four of the sixteen have a Next bridge route built for them, so dev plumbing was written for endpoints nobody calls: /api/angle/find, /api/consensus-edge/health, /api/rankings/sources, /api/sharp/roster-percentage/audit.

reproduction.command: cat /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W01/dead-routes.txt ; grep -rn 'test-alert' /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket --include='*.py' --include='*.js' --include='*.jsx' --include='*.yml' --include='*.sh' | grep -v node_modules | grep -v master-site-audit
reproduction.expected: Every advertised route has at least one production consumer.
reproduction.actual: 16 routes with only test callers; `grep test-alert` returns only its own definition at server.py:9779.

userImpact: No direct user impact — these routes are invisible. The cost is to maintainers and to this audit: CLAUDE.md's API table lists scaffold endpoints as product surface, so a reader budgets attention for a pipeline-introspection feature that has no UI and, per PRIOR-A23-F15, no producer either.

priorFinding.note: The prior finding established that /api/scaffold/* has no producer. This adds the other half — it has no consumer either — and extends the census to 16 routes across five subsystems.

whatWorks: The census itself: openapi.json from the live app is an accurate authoritative route list, and every route that IS wired resolves to a real page or component (72 of 99).
rootCause: Routes outlive their consumers. There is no CI check that a registered route is referenced by something other than a test.
requiredRepair: Delete POST /api/test-alert. Decide per-route for the rest: retire, or wire. Add a test that walks the OpenAPI schema and asserts every path is referenced by frontend code, a workflow, a systemd unit, or an explicit OPS_ONLY allowlist — the same shape as tests/api/test_feature_flag_reachability.py, which already does this successfully for flags.
dependencies: W01-F002 (gameplan), W01-F010 (scaffold/status is also a public info leak), W01-F011 (rankings/sources), W01-F012 (public-league CSV export).

title: Two of four navigation surfaces ignore the adminOnly flag: /more and the command palette render Admin, Source Health, ROS Data Health and Trade Coverage to a session with isAdmin false
claimUnderTest: nav-model.js states the rule outright: 'Ops surfaces are ADMIN-ONLY in the nav. ... the menu showed all four to every signed-in user — so a guest-pass holder saw a "Admin" entry, clicked it, and got a wall. Offering a door that is always locked is worse than not showing the door.' systemItemsFor({isAdmin}) exists to enforce it.
observed: Only frontend/components/shell/TopBar.jsx:58 and frontend/components/shell/MobileChrome.jsx:106 call systemItemsFor({isAdmin}). frontend/app/more/page.jsx builds `[...NAV_MODEL, SYSTEM_MODEL]` and maps `group.items` directly, unfiltered — it imports SYSTEM_MODEL but not systemItemsFor. frontend/components/shell/CommandPalette.jsx:42 calls paletteTargets(), which spreads all of SYSTEM_MODEL.items with no isAdmin argument available to it. Fetched live with the e2e-test-user session (/api/auth/status returns isAdmin:false), the /more HTML contains 'Source Health', 'ROS Data Health', 'Trade Coverage' and '>Admin<' with their hrefs. This is not a hydration flash — no code path in either component ever filters.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/auth/status; curl -s -H "Cookie: jason_session=$SID" http://127.0.0.1:3001/more | grep -o 'Source Health\|ROS Data Health\|Trade Coverage\|>Admin<' | sort -u; grep -rn 'systemItemsFor' /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/frontend/app /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/frontend/components
reproduction.expected: Zero admin entries in /more for a session with isAdmin:false; systemItemsFor called by all four navigation surfaces.
reproduction.actual: auth_status isAdmin:false, yet /more renders all four Ops entries. systemItemsFor is called from exactly 2 files (TopBar.jsx, MobileChrome.jsx) out of 4 navigation surfaces.

userImpact: A guest-pass holder or any non-admin signed-in user still sees four Ops destinations — on /more and in the command palette, which is the fastest navigation path in the app. Clicking Admin yields a 200 shell that then renders 'This page requires an admin session'. That is exactly the locked door the code comment says it removed, and it also discloses the operator tool inventory.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced at HEAD e96c06ef with a live non-admin session. Still open on both surfaces named by the prior finding.

whatWorks: The desktop top bar and the mobile drawer both filter correctly. The server side is sound: every /api/admin/* route 403s a non-admin, and /admin degrades to an explicit 'requires an admin session' card rather than a blank or a fake dashboard. /admin's feature-flag panel is read-only and even renders gateStatus with an honest tooltip.
rootCause: systemItemsFor is an opt-in helper rather than a property of the model. Three consumers had to remember to call it; two did.
requiredRepair: Make paletteTargets accept {isAdmin} and filter SYSTEM_MODEL through systemItemsFor; have /more call systemItemsFor({isAdmin}) from useAuthContext (it already reads that context for the sign-out button). Extend frontend/__tests__/nav-model to assert every SYSTEM_MODEL consumer filters — the coverage invariant that file already pins is the right place.

title: Three pages are reachable from no navigation at all — /finder, /intel and /design — and /design is a dev-only design-system gallery shipped in the production build
claimUnderTest: nav-model.js says it is the 'Single source of truth for every navigation surface' and that /more 'can never drift from the real navigation'. Both are true — which is precisely why a page absent from the model is absent from every navigation surface simultaneously.
observed: 41 page.jsx files exist. 31 hrefs appear in NAV_MODEL + SYSTEM_MODEL + MOBILE_TABS_PUBLIC + PALETTE_EXTRA_TARGETS. Grepping every .js/.jsx under frontend/app and frontend/components for '/finder', '/design' and '/intel' outside those pages' own directories returns zero hits — no nav entry, no /more entry (it maps the same model), no palette target, no in-app Link. All three return 200 with a session and 307 to /login anonymously. /finder and /intel are self-documented legacy redirect shims and are fine as such. /design is different: it is a live DesignGallery route with no redirect, marked robots:{index:false}, present in the production Next build, and gated only by session presence — any signed-in user who guesses the URL gets it. Two further pages are deep-link-only by design and documented as such: /rankings/[position] (client redirect to /rankings?pos=X) and /draft-capital (308 to /league?tab=draft-capital, named in pageTitleFor but in no menu).

reproduction.command: grep -rn "/finder\|/design\|'/intel'\|\"/intel\"" /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/frontend/app /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/frontend/components /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/frontend/lib | grep -v 'app/finder/\|app/design/\|app/intel/' ; for p in /finder /design /intel; do printf '%s anon=%s auth=%s\n' $p $(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:3000$p) $(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H "Cookie: jason_session=$SID" http://127.0.0.1:3000$p); done
reproduction.expected: Either a nav/link reference, or the page not shipped.
reproduction.actual: Zero references. /finder anon=307 auth=200 · /design anon=307 auth=200 · /intel anon=307 auth=200

numericProof.formula: orphans = pages that appear in neither NAV_MODEL, SYSTEM_MODEL, MOBILE_TABS*, PALETTE_EXTRA_TARGETS, nor any <Link href>

userImpact: None for /finder and /intel — they are bookmark shims doing their job. For /design: a signed-in user who lands on it sees a full-fidelity board rendering fabricated player values (Justin Jefferson 9541 etc., per PRIOR-A06-F13) with no on-screen indication it is sample data.

priorFinding.note: The prior finding covers /design's fabricated content. This adds the reachability half — it is in no navigation, so nothing ever pointed at it, which is why the fabricated content was never noticed.

whatWorks: The nav model genuinely is the single source: /more, the palette, the top bar and the mobile drawer all derive from it, and all 31 nav hrefs resolve to a page that returns 200 with a session. Zero nav entries point at nothing. /finder and /intel both carry accurate comments explaining exactly what they redirect to and why.
rootCause: No test asserts the inverse of the nav coverage invariant. frontend/__tests__/nav-model pins 'every routable surface stays reachable' in one direction only; nothing asserts 'every page under app/ is either in the model, a documented shim, or explicitly excluded'.
requiredRepair: Exclude /design from the production build (move it behind an env guard or into a separate dev-only entry point), or add an unmistakable 'SAMPLE DATA' banner. Add the reverse coverage test: enumerate app/**/page.jsx and assert each path is in the nav model or on a named exclusion list.

title: Four names in the product vocabulary map to no route at all: IDP Lab does not exist, and Edge Finder, Roster Analyzer and Buy/Sell Tracker name nothing in the shipped IA
claimUnderTest: The audit brief and the user's working vocabulary name Rankings, Trade Calculator, Edge Finder, Angle, League, IDP Lab, Settings, More, Roster Analyzer, Trade Finder, Waivers, ROS, Buy/Sell Tracker, Consensus Edge, Sharp Tracker, Insider Trading, Draft, Player pages and Team pages as surfaces of this product.
observed: Mapped exhaustively in the artifact. 'IDP Lab' has ZERO occurrences anywhere in the repository — code, config, docs, tests — so it is Missing, not renamed. 'Edge Finder' names nothing; the nearest surface is /edge, relabelled 'Source Disagreement' by the #626 IA pass. 'Roster Analyzer' names nothing; its substance is split between /rosters ('Team Strength') and the unreachable GET /api/gameplan (W01-F002). 'Buy/Sell Tracker' is ambiguous — both /market/sharp-tracker and /consensus-edge answer to it and neither uses the name. 'Trade Finder' is now /arbitrage ('Arbitrage'), 'Angle' is now 'Package Builder', 'Signal Blotter'/'Finder' merged into the /rankings Screens dropdown, and 'Intel' was split into the Market and League groups. 'ROS' has seven backend routes and no page or nav entry of its own. The naming rule nav-model.js declares does hold: all 20 static pages' PageHeader title strings are byte-identical to their nav labels.

reproduction.command: grep -rniE 'idp lab|idp-lab|idplab' /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket --include='*.py' --include='*.js' --include='*.jsx' --include='*.md' | grep -v node_modules | grep -v master-site-audit ; cat /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W01/feature-name-map.md
reproduction.expected: A route or page for each named feature.
reproduction.actual: 'idp lab' matches only three unrelated lines about IDP position labelling in Dynasty Scraper.py and src/roster_intel/roster_source.py. No IDP Lab exists.

numericProof.formula: 13 exact + 4 renamed + 1 missing (IDP Lab) + 1 ambiguous (Buy/Sell Tracker) = 19

userImpact: The operator asks for work on a feature that does not exist, or asks for 'Edge Finder' and gets work on /edge, /arbitrage or /finder depending on who reads it. The #626 rename was correct and well-reasoned but no migration note maps old vocabulary to new, so every conversation re-derives it.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding addresses vocabulary-to-route mapping.

whatWorks: The IA rename itself is disciplined and the reasoning is recorded in nav-model.js. The label/h1/pageTitleFor invariant holds on all 20 static pages — the naming rule the file declares is genuinely enforced.
rootCause: The #626 rename changed labels without leaving an old-name → new-name index anywhere a human or an agent would look.
requiredRepair: Add the mapping table from feature-name-map.md to CLAUDE.md, including the four names that resolve to nothing, so the vocabulary gap is stated rather than rediscovered.

title: There is no private player page and no private team page — a player opens a modal with no URL, and the only real player/franchise pages live in the public-league subtree
claimUnderTest: The brief names 'Player pages' and 'Team pages' as product surfaces.
observed: The only routable player page is /league/player/[playerId] and the only routable team page is /league/franchise/[owner]; both are in the PUBLIC league subtree (public-routes.js PUBLIC_PREFIXES includes /league) and both are served by the isolated src/public_league/ pipeline, which by design never reads the private contract. On the private side — /rankings, /trade, /waivers, /draft, /rosters — a player opens frontend/components/PlayerPopup.jsx, a modal. It carries the richest per-player view in the app (rank history, per-source values, ROS values, realized points, playerctx, news) and it has no URL: it cannot be linked, shared, bookmarked, opened in a new tab, or reached by browser back. There is no /player/[id] or /team/[id] under frontend/app. The modal itself links OUT to the public /league/franchise/{ownerId} for ownership, so the private surface hands the user off to the public pipeline to see a team.

reproduction.expected: A private per-player and per-team route.
reproduction.actual: `ls` returns only `players` (which contains only `compare`). The only player/franchise pages found are under app/league/. PlayerPopup's only internal hrefs are /league/franchise/{ownerId} and /players/compare.

numericProof.formula: privateRoutes = |{app/**/page.jsx matching a per-player or per-team dynamic segment outside the /league public subtree}|

userImpact: A user cannot send a teammate a link to a player's analysis, cannot bookmark a player they are tracking, and loses the whole view on a page refresh. It also blocks the natural home for the unreachable /api/gameplan (W01-F002) and the seven orphaned /api/ros/* routes (W01-F008), both of which are per-team by construction.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding treats the absence of private player/team routes as a defect; PRIOR-A06-* audits PlayerPopup's contents, not its addressability.

whatWorks: The public-league player and franchise pages are real, server-rendered, have opengraph-image routes for link unfurls, and are correctly isolated from the private contract. PlayerPopup's content itself is rich and its outbound links work.
rootCause: The private surface was built modal-first. Nothing forces a per-entity view to be addressable, so it never became one.
requiredRepair: Add /player/[playerId] and /team/[ownerId] under the private tree rendering the same data PlayerPopup already assembles, and have the modal deep-link to them. That gives /api/gameplan and /api/ros/* a home in the same move.

title: The ROS subsystem exposes seven backend routes and has no page and no nav entry — its only dedicated surface is an admin-only diagnostics tool
claimUnderTest: The brief names 'ROS' as a product surface. src/ros/ registers seven routes, implying a feature.
observed: There is no /ros page and no 'ROS' entry in NAV_MODEL. The seven routes surface only as fragments: /tools/ros-data-health (marked adminOnly in SYSTEM_MODEL, so it is hidden from the top bar and mobile drawer for every non-admin — though /more and the palette still show it, see W01-F004), the PlayerPopup modal (which has no URL, see W01-F007), RosTradeFitPanel on /trade, and one section of the /league hub (frontend/app/league/sections/ros-team-strength.jsx). A non-admin user has no navigable destination that is about rest-of-season projections. Six of the seven routes additionally have no Next bridge, so none of these fragments works under `next dev` (W01-F001).

reproduction.expected: A nav entry or page for a seven-route subsystem.
reproduction.actual: nav-model.js mentions ROS only in the adminOnly '/tools/ros-data-health' entry. Consumers are: app/tools/ros-data-health/page.jsx, app/league/sections/ros-team-strength.jsx, components/PlayerPopup.jsx, components/RosTradeFitPanel.jsx, lib/ros-data.js, lib/ros-index.js.

userImpact: A user who wants rest-of-season projections has no way to find them. The data reaches them only incidentally — if they happen to open a player modal or scroll the /league hub. Seven routes' worth of engineering is discoverable only by accident.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A03-F04 and PRIOR-A02-F06 audit ROS numbers; none treats the subsystem's absence from the IA as a finding.

whatWorks: All seven routes return 200 authenticated and the four consuming fragments render. /tools/ros-data-health is a genuine, working diagnostics page.
rootCause: ROS shipped as an enrichment layer over other surfaces rather than as a destination, and the IA was never revisited once it grew to seven routes.
requiredRepair: Either add a ROS destination to NAV_MODEL (the My Team group is the natural home, beside Waivers) or accept it as pure enrichment and say so in CLAUDE.md — but not both silently.
dependencies: W01-F001 (six of seven routes are unbridged), W01-F004, W01-F007.

title: feature_flags._GATE_STATUS's claim that 7 of 15 flags cannot change a response is true — verified by booting a second backend with all seven forced ON and diffing 1,092 contract rows
claimUnderTest: _GATE_STATUS classifies 7 of 15 registered flags as SCRIPT_ONLY, UNREACHABLE or NO_GATE — i.e. flipping them cannot change any response byte — and the remaining 8 as LIVE.
observed: Confirmed by runtime differential, not by re-reading the import graph. A second FastAPI process was booted on port 8001 (port 8000 untouched, run_scraper neutralised before uvicorn start, nothing written outside docs/master-site-audit/ and the scratchpad). Boot A: defaults. Boot B: espn_injury_feed, usage_signals, depth_chart_validation, value_confidence_intervals, positional_tiers, unified_id_mapper and dynamic_source_weights all forced to 1. Across 1,092 contract rows, 0 rows changed rankDerivedValue, 0 changed canonicalConsensusRank, 0 fields appeared and 0 disappeared. The only non-timestamp difference in the entire 12 MB view=full payload was players.*.rankChange (621 non-zero → 0), and boot C (defaults, third cold boot) reproduced the same 0 — proving rankChange is a function of accumulated rank-history depth since boot, not of any flag. All 8 LIVE flags were then proven to change a response: consensus_edge 503→200 with a real 325-player board; bdvm_engine, realized_points_api and monte_carlo_trade each 200→503 feature_disabled; te_basis_conversion moves 135 of 1,092 rankDerivedValue (82 TE + 50 PICK + 3 collateral) and 627 canonicalConsensusRank; idp_scoring_fit + reception_scoring_fit move 293 of 709 league-adjusted factors; nfl_data_ingest is lazily imported at server.py:4424 and :11241 and is genuinely reachable, though unobservable here because nfl_data_py is deliberately absent (pre-declared non-finding).

reproduction.command: bash docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W01/w01_boot.sh /tmp/def.log & sleep 55; bash docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W01/w01_flagprobe.sh 8001 /tmp/flagA; bash docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W01/w01_kill.sh; bash docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W01/w01_boot.sh /tmp/flip.log RISKIT_FEATURE_ESPN_INJURY_FEED=1 RISKIT_FEATURE_USAGE_SIGNALS=1 RISKIT_FEATURE_DEPTH_CHART_VALIDATION=1 RISKIT_FEATURE_VALUE_CONFIDENCE_INTERVALS=1 RISKIT_FEATURE_POSITIONAL_TIERS=1 RISKIT_FEATURE_UNIFIED_ID_MAPPER=1 RISKIT_FEATURE_DYNAMIC_SOURCE_WEIGHTS=1 & sleep 55; bash docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W01/w01_flagprobe.sh 8001 /tmp/flagB; # then diff playersArray (displayName, rankDerivedValue, canonicalConsensusRank)
reproduction.expected: If the claim is true: zero value or rank changes between boot A and boot B.
reproduction.actual: 0 of 1092 rows changed. Control boot C confirms the one apparent difference (rankChange) is boot-state, not flags. tests/api/test_feature_flag_reachability.py: 36 passed in 44.72s on .venv Python 3.11.15.

numericProof.formula: rowsChanged = |{r : rankDerivedValue_A(r) != rankDerivedValue_B(r) or canonicalConsensusRank_A(r) != canonicalConsensusRank_B(r)}|

userImpact: None — this is the positive case. The registry tells the truth about itself, /api/status reports gateStatus beside enabled so 'on' and 'on and it matters' cannot be confused, and /admin's flag panel surfaces the same distinction to the operator with an explicit tooltip.

priorFinding.note: The prior finding is about a stale BDVM doc claiming the engine defaults OFF, not about _GATE_STATUS. No prior finding tests the gate-status claim. The one stale detail I did find is cosmetic: both feature_flags.py and the reachability test still say 'of 13 registered flags' while _DEFAULTS now holds 15. The 7/15 ratio and every per-flag classification are current.

whatWorks: Everything in this finding. This is the pattern the rest of the codebase should copy: a claim that would otherwise be an uncheckable comment was moved into data and pinned by a test that recomputes the import graph, and it survives an independent runtime differential.
requiredRepair: Update the two docstrings that still say '13 registered flags' to 15.

title: GET /api/scaffold/status is in the unauthenticated public allowlist, returns absolute server filesystem paths, and has no caller of any kind
claimUnderTest: server.py's comment above _PUBLIC_API_EXACT says the gate 'Closes the scrape risk: without this gate, curl /api/data from a stranger returns the full private rankings contract' — i.e. the allowlist is a deliberate, minimal set of endpoints with nothing private in them.
observed: /api/scaffold/status sits in _PUBLIC_API_EXACT (server.py:2754). Fetched with no cookie against the running backend it returns 200 and 756 bytes whose payload includes `"path": "/home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/data/raw_sources/raw_source_snapshot_20260420T194828Z.json"` — the _meta() helper at server.py:4823 stamps `str(path)` for four separate snapshot families. In production this discloses the deploy root, the data-directory layout, snapshot filenames and their timestamps to any anonymous caller. The endpoint has no UI caller, no bridge, no ops caller and no test caller — it is in the public allowlist and CLAUDE.md's API table while being reached by nothing.

reproduction.expected: 401, or a payload with no absolute filesystem paths.

numericProof.formula: absolutePathsInPayload = count of _meta() blocks emitting str(path) — raw_sources, ingest_validation, league, identity

userImpact: No user acts on a wrong number, so this is not P0. It is a reconnaissance aid: an anonymous caller learns the server's absolute deploy path and the exact naming and timing of the pipeline's on-disk artifacts, on an endpoint that exists for nobody.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced verbatim at HEAD e96c06ef against the live server. Adds that the endpoint additionally has zero callers, so removing it from the public allowlist breaks nothing.

whatWorks: The rest of the public allowlist is defensible and deliberately reasoned in-file: /api/draft-capital is public but redacts the proprietary rookie fields for anonymous callers (_redact_draft_capital_for_public), and /api/news carries no league-private data.
rootCause: _meta() was written for an operator view and the route was later added to the public allowlist without re-reading what it emits.
requiredRepair: Drop /api/scaffold/status from _PUBLIC_API_EXACT (nothing calls it, so there is no compatibility cost), or emit path.name only and delete the `path` key.

title: CLAUDE.md names GET /api/rankings/sources as the runtime check for source-registry lockstep, but nothing calls it at runtime — the only reference in the entire tree is its own Next bridge
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md, 'Registry lockstep': 'Runtime check: GET /api/rankings/sources returns the authoritative Python registry (proxied through frontend/app/api/rankings/sources/route.js). Parity test: tests/api/test_source_registry_parity.py parses the frontend JS and diffs against the Python registry.' Two mechanisms are described, one runtime and one static.
observed: grep for 'rankings/sources' across all of frontend/ excluding node_modules and .next returns exactly two hits: line 18 of the bridge route itself (building the backend URL) and a comment in frontend/app/api/news/route.js saying it mirrors that proxy convention. No page, component or hook fetches it. /settings, which is where the source registry is edited, reads the registry from the contract instead. The static parity test is real and does the work; the 'runtime check' is a route and a bridge with no runtime consumer. So of the two lockstep mechanisms documented, one exists and one is a route nobody calls.

reproduction.expected: At least one fetch call site outside app/api/.
reproduction.actual: 2 hits: app/api/rankings/sources/route.js:18 (its own URL builder) and app/api/news/route.js:15 (a comment).

numericProof.formula: runtimeCallSites = |{fetch call sites for /api/rankings/sources outside frontend/app/api/}|

userImpact: None directly. The cost is that a documented safety net does not exist: a reader of CLAUDE.md believes registry drift would be caught at runtime as well as at test time, and budgets trust accordingly. Only the static test actually guards it.
whatWorks: tests/api/test_source_registry_parity.py is real and does exactly what it claims — it parses frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js::RANKING_SOURCES and diffs it against src/api/data_contract.py::_RANKING_SOURCES. The lockstep invariant IS protected, just by one mechanism rather than two.
rootCause: The route was built for an operator-facing check that was never wired into a page.
requiredRepair: Either surface it (a 'source registry' panel on /settings or /tools/source-health is the obvious home) or correct CLAUDE.md to say the parity test is the only lockstep guard and delete the route and its bridge.

title: The public-league CSV export at GET /api/public/league/{section}.csv has no link anywhere in the UI while four other pages ship their own client-side CSV builders
claimUnderTest: A dedicated backend CSV route with its own test file (tests/public_league/test_csv_export.py) implies a download the user can reach.
observed: grep for '.csv' across frontend/app, frontend/components and frontend/lib returns four download sites, all client-side Blob builders assembling CSV in JavaScript from already-loaded rows: /rankings (chaseupside-rankings-<iso>.csv), /trade (trade-<iso>.csv), /idptc-rookies (dynasty-rookie-board-<n>.csv) and /draft (draft-review-<date>.csv). None of them calls /api/public/league/{section}.csv, and /league — the page the route serves — has no export control at all. The backend route is exercised only by tests/public_league/test_csv_export.py and test_server_routes.py, plus one e2e spec.

reproduction.expected: A link or fetch to /api/public/league/<section>.csv from /league.
reproduction.actual: Four client-side Blob CSV builders, zero references to the backend CSV route.

numericProof.formula: backendCsvRouteCallSites = |{fetch or href targeting /api/public/league/*.csv in frontend/}|

userImpact: A user browsing the public league hub cannot export any of its tables, while a backend endpoint that would do exactly that exists, is tested and is public. Two implementations of 'export to CSV' exist and the reachable one is the client-side reimplementation.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers the CSV export split.

whatWorks: The four client-side exports work and produce sensibly-named files. The backend route responds correctly when called directly.
rootCause: The backend export shipped for the public-league pipeline; the UI export need arose separately on private pages and was solved client-side. Neither knew about the other.
requiredRepair: Add an export control to the /league hub tables wired to the existing backend route, or retire the route.
